findings.title: Direct Git-Sourced Dependency 'grunt-if' (Mutable Branch)
findings.explanation: Package 'grunt-if' is sourced directly from a Git repository ('https://github.com/binarymist/grunt-if/tarball/master') rather than a registered package registry. The specification references a mutable branch, which poses reproducibility and upstream drift risks. However, if package-lock.json resolves this reference to an immutable commit hash or integrity checksum, the local installation is frozen.
findings.technical_explanation: Package 'grunt-if' is sourced directly from a Git repository ('https://github.com/binarymist/grunt-if/tarball/master') rather than a registered package registry. The specification references a mutable branch, which poses reproducibility and upstream drift risks. However, if package-lock.json resolves this reference to an immutable commit hash or integrity checksum, the local installation is frozen.
findings.potential_impact: Minimal risk when pinned to full commit SHA; mutable branches or tags can introduce upstream changes between builds if lockfile is regenerated.
findings.recommended_action: Pin Git dependencies to full 40-character commit SHAs or vendor with subresource integrity digests.

supporting_evidence.detail: bcrypt-nodejs is an established legacy package on npm intended to provide pure-JS bcrypt support without requiring native build tools like node-gyp.

contradicting_evidence.detail: The edit distance and naming similarity alone do not indicate malicious squatting given the package's long history and known functionality.

ai_investigations.recommended_action: Migrate dependency from 'bcrypt-nodejs' to the modern, actively maintained 'bcrypt' package.

findings.remediation: Declare explicit least-privilege permissions (`permissions: contents: read`) to ensure deterministic access controls across all runner environments.

findings.title: First-party (official) Action 'actions/checkout' is not pinned to a commit SHA
findings.subject: actions/checkout@v2
findings.why: Tags are mutable references: while official GitHub/first-party actions have audited release processes, Pinning to a full 40-character commit SHA ensures immutable execution.
findings.remediation: Pin to the full 40-character commit SHA: `uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # v2`.

findings.title: Action 'actions/checkout@v2' is an outdated major version
findings.subject: actions/checkout@v2#outdated
findings.why: This major runs on an end-of-life Node.js runtime or was deprecated/shut down by GitHub; it no longer receives fixes and may stop working.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to actions/checkout@v4 or newer (pinned to a commit SHA).

ai_investigations.specific_suspicion_resolved: Confirmed that actions/checkout is unpinned and uses a mutable version tag.
remaining_security_risks: Vulnerability to tag reassignment or upstream compromise of the 'v2' reference.

observed_facts: Initial finding SUSP-CICD-GHA001-E2E_TEST-L21 (Docker & CI/CD) flagged in '.github/workflows/e2e-test.yml' at line 21: First-party (official) Action 'actions/setup-node' is not pinned to a commit SHA.
Recorded evidence snippet: uses: actions/setup-node@v1.
Workflow security: permissions block=False, third-party actions=0.
Source snippet confirmed in '.github/workflows/e2e-test.yml' lines 16-26.
ai_investigations.attack_scenario: An attacker with compromised access to the upstream official repository or ability to manipulate tags could retarget the 'v1' tag to point to a malicious commit, causing arbitrary code execution within the repository's CI/CD pipeline upon subsequent workflow runs.
ai_investigations.rationale: The workflow configuration at '.github/workflows/e2e-test.yml' utilizes the official GitHub Action 'actions/setup-node@v1' pinned only to a mutable major version tag ('@v1') rather than an immutable full-length commit SHA. While the action is first-party and trusted, relying on mutable tags exposes the pipeline to supply chain risks if the tag is ever overwritten or compromised upstream.

supporting_evidence.detail: Action 'actions/setup-node@v1' is referenced via a mutable version tag instead of a commit SHA.

contradicting_evidence.detail: The action is maintained by GitHub ('actions/'), which significantly lowers the likelihood of malicious intent compared to third-party actions.

ai_investigations.recommended_action: Pin the GitHub Action 'actions/setup-node' to its immutable full-length commit SHA (e.g., actions/setup-node@<commit-sha>) to ensure reproducible and secure builds.
